response: {"headline": "IMPROVE-IT met its primary endpoint in 18,144 ACS patients (ezetimibe/simvastatin vs simvastatin), but the magnitude of benefit and on-trial LDL-C difference remain unpublished as of the 2014-11-17 data cutoff.", "summary": "The phase 3 IMPROVE-IT trial randomized 18,144 acute coronary syndrome patients to ezetimibe/simvastatin or simvastatin monotherapy, targeting 5,250 primary endpoint events over a median 2.5-year follow-up. Merck announced the trial met its primary composite endpoint of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, unstable angina rehospitalization, coronary revascularization (≥30 days), or stroke. However, no hazard ratio, confidence interval, or on-treatment LDL-C difference in the IMPROVE-IT population has been verified in the available facts.
